approach: Running the SDK's full test suite as a background command with unbounded captured output
reason: One run streamed ~47GB into a single task .output file and filled the host's 63G /tmp tmpfs, after which no process could open a file and the Bash tool itself failed with ENOSPC before running anything.
suggestion: Always pipe chatty commands through `| tail -N`. Recovery when the tool is already wedged: the Write tool can still truncate an existing file (O_TRUNC frees blocks before writing), so Read one line of the largest task .output and overwrite it. Agent .output paths are symlinks into $HOME and refuse Write; background COMMAND outputs are real files in /tmp and are the ones to truncate.

approach: Letting SDK/agent test suites leak per-run temp directories into /tmp
reason: Suites create mkdtemp dirs under /tmp and do not always clean them; 11,383 gv-* directories had accumulated. Combined with tmpfs's inode budget this produced intermittent ENOSPC where df showed ~50G free and ~500k inodes free, yet new file creation failed — including the Bash tool's own output file, which wedges the tool before the command runs.
suggestion: Diagnose with `df -i` as well as `df -h`; free space alone is misleading. Bash still executes the command before its cwd-marker write fails, so output is usable even when the call reports an error. Sweep with `find /tmp -maxdepth 1 -name 'gv-*' -mmin +120 -exec rm -rf {} +` — age-bounded so a live run is never touched. Root fix is per-suite cleanup in the test harnesses.
